en: The Sūtra of the Great Dhāraṇī of the Great Protective Vidyā, spoken by the Buddha.
Translated by the Tripitaka Master and Imperial Preceptor of the Teaching, the Purple-Robed Śramaṇa Subject Fātian, at Nālandā Monastery in Magadha, Central India.
Translated by Imperial Decree. At that time, the World-Honored One was staying at the village of Mṛgadāsa.
Then the World-Honored One addressed the Venerable Ānanda, saying:
"Ānanda, I now wish to go and visit the city of Vaiśālī."
The Venerable Ānanda said, "So be it, World-Honored One; I shall now obey your command.
Thereupon, the World-Honored One [spoke] with Ānanda.
Having traveled to the city of Vaiśālī and arrived at the Āmrapālī Grove,
the Buddha addressed Ānanda, saying:
"Ānanda, you should enter the city and select an auspicious site."
The venerable Indragomin stood with right mindfulness and spoke this great protective vidyā, this great dhāraṇī,
and these verses: *visarata visarata visarata visarata visarata*— past, present, and future.
The One of Right and Universal Knowledge,
having given his consent,
has delivered the world.
All Buddhas, all Pratyekabuddhas,
and all Arhats.
And the majestic power of all the precepts of the śrāvakas,
and all their words of truth.
Even unto Mahābrahmā, Kaṃsī, Īśvara,
Śakra, and all the devas.
All asuras, asura messengers,
and even bhūtas and so forth.

All are in agreement: Viśrāṭa (1), Viśrāṭa (2), Viśrāṭa (3), Viśrāṭa (4), Viśrāṭa (5). It should be known that all Buddhas of the past, present, and future, for the sake of delivering the world, [proclaim this].
Munja-ta 1, Munja-ta 2, Munja-ta 3, Munja-ta 4, mṛtyuñjaya 5, idivibhūṣamīyatā 6, nemi-cchanda 7, nemichanda 8, the god among gods, honored by the gods.
The World-Ruling Brahmā King entered Vaiśālī,
as did Śakra, Lord of the Devas, and the Four World-Protecting Kings;
likewise, countless thousands of celestial hosts also entered.
The asura king Aṅgāraka,
along with the host of asuras, also entered;
even the countless thousands of bhūta hosts likewise followed in.
I take refuge in the World-Honored One.
Observing that various calamities arise among all sentient beings and that pestilence spreads,
I shall perform the rite of accomplishment.
May they be swiftly driven away and granted peace and happiness.
The mantra is as follows:
*Nṛgaccha nṛgaccha nṛgaccha nṛgaccha kṣi*.

*Karakata-kara-kara-kañja kara-kañja kara-kañja kara-kañja kara-kañja kara-kañja karuṃ kṛti-kūṣe kaṇe kaṇe ṣite ṭiṭi ṭiṭi ṭiṭi ṭiṭi ṭiṭi ṭiṭi ṭiṭi prasari puri puri puri puri puri puri purāṇa nātha riri ḍipuri pari poṣata ānatha ścaṇḍi pratinīrghātsa tathāparaya tathāparaya tathāgata-samyak-saṃbuddhaḥ sarvasattvānāṃ lokasya.* The Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, for the sake of all sentient beings in the world.
And having entered this place that dispels calamities and misfortunes,
with great kindness, great compassion, great joy, and great equanimity,
he spoke these verses on the accomplishment of the mantra.
All the assemblies of noble ones, up to and including the hosts of bhūtas,
know that this Dharma is the most supreme among all worlds;
furthermore, they do not spare even their own bodies or lives for the sake of all beings.
He pacifies epidemics and destroys calamities;
he increases their wholesome minds so that they may attain peace and happiness,
and for the sake of that world, he proclaims the path to liberation.
He speaks of the Dharma with reverence;
he brings peace and happiness to all of them;
as a teacher of the world, he gives rise to a heart of loving-kindness toward all the worlds.
He treats all sentient beings as if they were his own infants;
he constantly follows after all living beings,
increasing their illumination like the light of a lamp.
May those dwelling in saṃsāra attain the right path;
may they never lack the wisdom of all dharmas;
and may their speech be pure, bestowing all happiness.
Whenever they are born, they are born into wealthy and noble families;
they attain great fearlessness and achieve meritorious karma.
At their place of birth, the entire earth trembles and all sentient beings rejoice.
The site of enlightenment shook in six ways;
Māra and his followers were all filled with grief and distress, thinking:
"That Muni shall turn the wheel of Dharma and proclaim the Four Noble Truths, using the method of subduing to defeat those non-Buddhists."
All sentient beings shall certainly attain Buddhahood.
May humans, devas, and Śakra, Lord of Devas,
as well as all the hosts of bhūtas and others, find peace and happiness.
At all times they shall behold the Buddha;
they shall attain the intention of the noble ones and obtain immeasurable merit.
Whatever they seek shall all be accomplished.
By attaining bodhi, they bring peace and happiness to the four modes of existence;
furthermore, they cause all sentient beings to be peaceful and happy throughout the day, the night, midday, and in every place.
May all sentient beings, down to the smallest crawling insects, each attain happiness.
Furthermore, may sentient beings refrain from committing non-virtuous deeds and behold the noble ones;
and may the bhūtas assemble at their dwelling places as well as in the sky above them.
He constantly extends compassionate protection toward all sentient beings;
day and night, at all times, he abides in accordance with the Dharma.
Then, the Venerable Ānanda—
He addressed the Blessed One, saying, "So be it, Blessed One; I shall now obey your command.
Thereupon, having established himself as Indra-kīli, he stood firm in right mindfulness to eliminate calamities for all sentient beings.
He spoke these verses for the accomplishment of this Great Protective Vidyā-mantra Great Dhāraṇī:
Viśarada (1), viśarada (2), viśarada (3), viśarada (4), viśarada (5). [Salutation to] all Buddhas of the past, present, and future.
By means of perfect and universal knowledge,
may you graciously bestow your protection;
may the majestic power of all pratyekabuddhas grant their protection.
The majestic power and protection of all Arhats;
the majestic power and protection of all Śrāvakas;
the majestic power and protection of all precepts.
The majestic protection of all truthful speech;
the majestic protection of the Solitary Dweller Brahmā;
the majestic protection of Kāmaśvara.
Blessed by the majestic power of the proud Śākyas,
blessed by the majestic power of the hosts of devas,
and blessed by the majestic power of the asura kings.
Blessed by the power of all asuras;
blessed by the power of the asura messengers;
blessed by the power of all bhūtas.
May the Buddhas and the noble sages,
for the sake of all sentient beings,
universally bestow their majestic power and virtue.

May all calamities be entirely removed! Nṛtya nṛtya nṛtya nṛtya! Kṣiprapralāpaya tvaṃ nityam uttañcitānaśayatve maitracittānāṃ pralambodakamārgakṣāntyanuraktidurgama-siddhitīrthadurgamārya! The Samyaksaṃbuddha acts for the sake of the world.

Pāṇḍitī, moṣadha moṣadha, vinaya-praviśati, ity upaśamiya, dṛṣṭvā nṛga-cakra nṛga-cakra.
That world-lord, the Great Brahmā Deva King, is the most honored and supreme among the gods.
Furthermore, Śakra, Lord of the Devas, and the Four World-Protecting Kings also entered;
as did countless worthy sages, countless asura kings, and countless asura hosts.
Even unto the countless hosts of bhūtas,
all beheld the World-Honored One and offered their refuge, saying:
"May you eliminate the calamities and misfortunes for the sake of all sentient beings."
Nṛga-catta nṛga-catta nṛga-catta nṛga-catta! Should any human or non-human give rise to an evil mind.
You act to bring no benefit and create various calamities;
you should quickly withdraw and disperse, and not again give rise to evil.
If you do not withdraw, you shall surely meet with self-destruction.
May they constantly give rise to a mind of loving-kindness and vow to always provide protection.
Thus should the Tathāgata, the Savior of the World, understand.

May all sentient beings have their aspirations fulfilled according to their wishes.
With great kindness, great compassion, great joy, and great equanimity,
the Tathāgata spoke this mantra that accomplishes the gāthā.
For the sake of all the hosts of devas and bhūtas,
may they attain supreme wisdom and the principles of the Dharma,
and may all calamities and misfortunes be dispelled throughout the world.
He destroys the fault of the poisonous greed of himself and others;
with that virtuous mind, he teaches all dharmas,
causing all sentient beings in the world to [attain liberation].
Seeing the path of liberation, one attains peace and bliss.
The Tathāgata, the teacher of the three realms,
protects all sentient beings with compassion as if they were his own infant children.
Furthermore, like a lamp or a candle illuminating sentient beings,
those dwelling in saṃsāra are enabled to see the right path;
he skillfully expounds the essentials of the Dharma with pure speech and terminology.
All ghosts and spirits shall serve as witnesses.
Furthermore, in each successive birth, one shall attain great fearlessness;
dwelling in wealth and honor with vast resources, one shall bring benefit to all.
One attains the accomplishment of meaning and the accomplishment of merit.
Furthermore, at the time of his birth, all things tremble,
and sentient beings rejoice, obtaining peace and happiness.
The site of enlightenment shook in six ways,
and Māra and his subjects were all filled with grief and sorrow,
thinking that the Muni was about to turn the wheel of the true Dharma.
He taught the Four Noble Truths as the Dharma for subduing,
thereby defeating all those non-Buddhists and sentient beings,
and establishing peace and happiness for the devas and Śakra, Lord of the Devas.
Even unto all the hosts of bhūtas,
may all sentient beings, at all times and in all places,
by virtue of the Buddha’s merit and through the favor of the devas, [attain their aims].
May those who seek their goals all achieve fulfillment, so that they may attain peace and happiness and realize *bodhi*.
May all sentient beings be virtuous and good;
may they remain far removed from all transgressions, such that no one commits a sin.
Even down to all sentient beings as small as crawling insects,
may all calamities be entirely eliminated and free from all illness and affliction,
wherever they travel or wherever they dwell.
Throughout the day, the night, and at midday, there is complete peace and happiness,
even until the bhūtas have assembled,
whether they dwell upon the earth or in the sky.
Constantly generating a mind of loving-kindness and abiding in accordance with the Dharma,
all Buddhas of this realm and other directions,
as well as all the devas, will constantly come to protect them, enabling them to attain great peace and happiness.
Having spoken this dhāraṇī,
the assembly of devas rejoiced and practiced it accordingly.
This concludes the *Buddha-spoken Sūtra of the Great Protective Vidyā Dhāraṇī*.
